Subject: Renewal runway: co-term + phased capacity options

Hi Ben —

Hope you had a good weekend. As we approach your Oct 31 renewal window, I wanted to put a few concrete options on the table so your procurement and platform teams can pick the path that minimizes disruption to Acme's launch schedule. Quick summary up front: we can co-term to Acme’s fiscal year, offer a 36-month blended discount with staged ramp buckets, or keep a 12-month contract with an early-burst add-on and auto-renew.

Options (high level):
- Option A — Co-term to 10/31/2028 (36 months): graduated discounts at 12/24/36 months, committed baseline with quarterly true-ups. Good if you want price predictability and a lower unit rate over time.
- Option B — 12-month + frontloaded burst: keep 12-month term, offer upfront credits for onboarding + two burst windows in Q1 and Q3. Fits teams that expect big short-term experiments.
- Option C — 24-month hybrid with auto-renew opt-out: mid-level discount, a staged ramp schedule (20/50/80% of committed capacity by month 3/9/18), and an explicit 60-day opt-out before renewal.

Questions for your team:
1) Would Acme prefer co-term to FY or stay on calendar anniversary?
2) Is a guaranteed baseline (committed units) required, or can we rely on a committed minimum + overage?
3) Any procurement constraints on auto-renew language?

I've attached a draft MOU and a recommended phased_ramp_schedule.xlsx with token-band examples and milestone-based credit release tied to onboarding. If it helps, we can map the staged ramp to your product launch milestones and build a mutual action plan.

Next steps: if you can share (a) procurement's preferred term length and (b) a rough launch timeline, I’ll convert Option A/B/C into a single-page mutual action plan and an executable amendment.

Thanks — look forward to aligning.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Renewal runway: co-term + phased capacity options

Vanessa, thanks for laying this out — very helpful. A few quick items from our side:

- Procurement prefers co-terming to our fiscal year if pricing is neutral to slightly favorable; a 36-month structure would be fine if we get annual checkpoints.
- For capacity, we want a ramp that supports our Q1 product launch — that means ~50% of target capacity by month 3, and full capacity by month 9. The staged ramp sheet looks like the right approach.
- Auto-renew is okay as long as there is an explicit opt-out and a true-up window (60 days is reasonable).

We also need a simple clause around overage billing cadence — monthly invoicing is preferred. Purchasing is looped for any T&C redlines. If you can produce a MOU with three clear paths (Co-term 36m, 24m hybrid, 12m + burst) and estimated unit economics for each, I’ll get it routed to legal and procurement this week.

Thanks —
Ben
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme AI
ben.jacobs@acme.ai

Team — looping you both to recommend a single play we send to Acme this afternoon. My suggested approach (to balance revenue predictability + expansion upside):

1) Present Option C as the primary proposal: 24-month hybrid with staged ramp (20/50/80% by M3/M9/M18), auto-renew allowed with 60-day opt-out, monthly invoicing for overages.
2) Include Option A (36-month co-term) as an alternative that offers a deeper discount and annual checkpoints — useful if Acme chooses price certainty.
3) Keep Option B (12m + frontloaded burst) as a fast-start add-on for Q1 experimentation; priced as a short-term credit package layered on top of the primary term.

Rationale: Option C gives us a credible upsell path at M9 when they hit full capacity; it also surfaces a clear checkpoint for Marissa to propose a mid-term performance review and potential uplift. Financials: use the phased_ramp_schedule.xlsx and tie a 10% onboarding credit release to the M3 milestone.

Can Marissa confirm acceptable discount bands so I can finalize the commercial numbers? Vanessa — if you’re good with the language on the auto-renew opt-out I’ll draft the amendment and include a short mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Renewals Strategy | Redwood Inference
